$data.description: Reusable pull-request facts supplied by a review harness.

pull-request.description: One observed pull request, including its Markdown author description, revision, diff statistics, and checks.

instructions.producer:
Replace the complete source whenever the pull request or its checks change:

```bash
leaf data set "$PAGE" <source-id> --file pull-request.json
```

The JSON object carries `repository`, positive integer `number`, `title`, `author`, `base`, `head`, `revision`, `status`, a Markdown `description`, RFC 3339 `observedAt`, a `diff` object counting the change's `files`, `additions`, `deletions`, and `commits`, and a `checks` map from check name to status. Keep the source id on the same pull request for the page's lifetime. Leaf presents these supplied facts; it does not query a forge.

description.description: The author's pull-request description as Markdown. Raw HTML is displayed as text.

lf-pull-request.description: A commentable account of a pull request, including the original author’s description and observed checks.
lf-pull-request.x-instructions: Place one empty element before the agent-authored walkthrough and bind it to the page's pull-request source. The widget labels the original author description, so surrounding prose can carry the reviewer's analysis.

lf-call-diff.description: A commentable unified call-tree diff with links to its exact patch evidence.
lf-call-diff.x-instructions:
Select the diff package beside pr-review, and point diff at the lf-diff holding the exact patch. Supply authentic CallDiff plain-text output as the source’s string value:

```bash
jq -Rs . calldiff.txt | leaf data set "$PAGE" <source-id>
```

Keep unchanged tree items as stable comparison landmarks. Prefer one focused file or entry point per widget for a large repository. Do not transcribe the output into markup, invent attribute reads as calls, or redraw separate before-and-after diagrams.
